You can create a page by default exporting a component from the file: 00007| 00008| ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 00009| export default function Page({ 00010| params, 00011| searchParams, 00012| }: { 00013| params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 00014| searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 00015| }) { 00016| return

My Page

00023| } 00024| ``` 00025| 00026| ## Good to know 00027| 00028| - The `.js`, `.jsx`, or `.tsx` file extensions can be used for `page`. 00029| - A `page` is always the **leaf** of the route subtree. 00030| - A `page` file is required to make a route segment **publicly accessible**. 00031| - Pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default, but can be set to a [Client Component](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client). 00032| - In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `page.js` is the innermost file convention. - **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

description: API reference for the not-found.js file.

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. `next/image` changes 00661| 00662| ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 00663| 00664| Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 00665| 00666| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 00667| import Image from 'next/image' 00668| 00669| export default function Page() { 00670| return 00671| } 00672| ``` 00673| 00674| If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 00675| 00676| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00677| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00678| 00679| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00680| images: { 00681| localPatterns: [ 00682| { 00683| pathname: '/assets/**', 00684| search: '?v=1', 00685| }, 00686| ], 00687| }, 00688| } 00689| 00690| export default nextConfig 00691| ``` 00692| 00693| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00694| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00695| const nextConfig = { 00696| images: { 00697| localPatterns: [ 00698| { 00699| pathname: '/assets/**', 00700| search: '?v=1', 00701| }, 00702| ], 00703| }, 00704| } 00705| 00706| module.exports = nextConfig 00707| ``` 00708| 00709| ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 00710| 00711| The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00712| 00713| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 00714| 00715| Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 00716| 00717| If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 00718| 00719| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 00720| import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 00721| 00722| const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 00723| images: { 00724| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00725| }, 00726| } 00727| 00728| export default nextConfig 00729| ``` 00730| 00731| ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 00732| /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 00733| const nextConfig = { 00734| images: { 00735| minimumCacheTTL: 60, 00736| }, 00737| } 00738| 00739| module.exports = nextConfig 00740| ``` 00741| 00742| ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 00743| 00744| The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 00745| 00746| We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 00960| 00961| ## Scroll Behavior Override 00962| 00963| In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 00964| 00965| 1. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 00972| 00973| **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 00974| 00975| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 00976| export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 00977| return ( 00978| 00979| {children} 00980| 00981| ) 00982| } 00983| ``` 00984| 00985| ## Performance Improvements 00986| 00987| Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 00988| 00989| **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 00990| 00991| The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 00992| 00993| ### `next dev` config load 00994| 00995| In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 00996| 00997| - When running the `next dev` command 00998| - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 00999| 01000| This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 01001| 01002| A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 01003| 01004| > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 01005| 01006| This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. title: How to upgrade to version 16
nav_title: Version 16
description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16.

{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}

## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded.

Give the agent this prompt:

```prompt
Upgrade this app to Next.js 16.

Before editing code, make sure AGENTS.md points at version-matched Next.js docs. If it is missing or outdated, follow [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs), then read AGENTS.md.

Then follow the [Next.js 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16) as the source of truth for the migration. Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#using-the-codemod) when you're ready to run the mechanical upgrade.

This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00712| 00713| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 00714| 00715| Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 00712| 00713| For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. ## Use an AI agent (recommended)

An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Upgrade this app to Next.js 16.

00002| title: layout.js
00003| description: API reference for the layout.js file.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.
00007| 
00008| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
00009| export default function DashboardLayout({
00010|   children,
00011| }: {
00012|   children: React.ReactNode
00013| }) {
00014|   return <section>{children}</section>
00015| }
00016| ```
00017| 
00018| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
00019| export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
00020|   return <section>{children}</section>
00021| }
00022| ```
00023| 
00024| In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
00025| 
00026| A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
00027| 
00028| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00029| export default function RootLayout({
00030|   children,
00031| }: {
00032|   children: React.ReactNode
00033| }) {
00034|   return (
00035|     <html lang="en">
00036|       <body>{children}</body>
00037|     </html>
00038|   )
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00043| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00044|   return (
00045|     <html lang="en">
00046|       <body>{children}</body>
00047|     </html>
00048|   )
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ## Reference
00053| 
00054| ### Props
00055| 
00056| #### `children` (required)
00057| 
00058| Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
00059| 
00060| #### `params` (optional)
00061| 
00062| A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout.
00063| 
00064| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher
00065| export default async function Layout({
00066|   children,
00067|   params,
00068| }: {
00069|   children: React.ReactNode
00070|   params: Promise<{ team: string }>
00071| }) {
00072|   const { team } = await params
00073| }
00074| ```
00075| 
00076| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
00077| export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
00078|   const { team } = await params
00079| }
00080| ```
00081| 
00082| | Example Route                     | URL            | `params`                           |
00083| | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
00084| | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
00085| | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
00086| | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
00087| 
00088| - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.
00089|   - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
00090| 
00091| ### Layout Props Helper
00092| 
00093| You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper.
00094| 
00095| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
00096| export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
00097|   return (
00098|     <section>
00099|       {props.children}
00100|       {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */}
00101|       {/* {props.analytics} */}
00102|     </section>
00103|   )
00104| }
00105| ```
00106| 
00107| > **Good to know**:
00108| >
00109| > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
00110| > - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
00111| 
00112| ### Root Layout
00113| 
00114| The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`.
00115| 
00116| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00117| export default function RootLayout({
00118|   children,
00119| }: {
00120|   children: React.ReactNode
00121| }) {
00122|   return (
00123|     <html>
00124|       <body>{children}</body>
00125|     </html>
00126|   )
00127| }
00128| ```
00129| 
00130| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00131| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00132|   return (
00133|     <html>
00134|       <body>{children}</body>
00135|     </html>
00136|   )
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| - The root layout **must** define `<html>` and `<body>` tags.
00141|   - You should **not** manually add `<head>` tags such as `<title>` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements.
00142| - You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches:
00143|   - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js`
00144|   - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories.
00145|   - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation).
00146| - The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. Dynamic segments before the root layout are **root parameters** and can be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params).
00147| 
00148| ## Caveats

00038|   )

00048|   )
00049| }
